doc: Tags over the Hierarchical Requirement Designer's binding, hierarchical-requirement.fbl#markdown, in the Markdown file (User Story 7; FR-026, FR-027, FR-028). tags is a word slot of the group words, with many (hierarchical-requirement.des: string, many), so it holds every #name word of the group in order (FBL 0.7 section 4.6). read lists it as a JSON array of the items: FBL section 15.3 names a string, a number, a bool and null, and leaves a list's form open. The tags the input carries, in the order of their first appearance, are security (spelt #Security on REQ-0003), ux (#UX on REQ-0004), self-service and privacy; with no registration they are the implicit members of the tag list (DESL 0.2 section 7.7.2), which hierarchical-requirement-tag-list states over this same body. Each step is one operation of hierarchical-requirement.des, given as the model changes it makes, and is followed by its undo, so every step starts from the input. The fixture format gives an edit one model change (FBL section 15.3), and an operation over several carriers is one transaction of several (FBL section 6.4): such a step's edit holds its first change, and x-transaction names the operation and lists every change in the order it makes them. An operation that also changes the tag list (a new tag, a rename, a delete) writes the registration in the same edit (DESL 0.2 section 5.5, FBL 0.7 section 8.4); one fixture shows one file, so this one shows the Markdown file's splices only, and hierarchical-requirement-tag-list shows the registration's, as each step says. The file has CRLF endings.

attributes.title: A user signs in with an e-mail address and a password.
A password has at least twelve characters.
A session ends after 30 minutes without activity.
A user changes their own e-mail address.

steps.doc: addTag on ITEM-0002 with the name Security, typed: it equals the member security in any case, an implicit member, so the operation picks it with the list's spelling and creates no tag (FR-027): one set of tags, so only the Markdown file is written. ITEM-0002 has no word: the new item of the many slot tags is an insert-key of one space and the word, at the start of the group words, since no word of the group is held by tags or by a slot listed before it, and the empty group starts where the title Sessions ends (FBL 0.7 section 6.3, lines and blocks, a word a set adds).

steps.doc: addTag on REQ-0005 with the name security: its author wrote state:rejected before #privacy, which reads the same, since the trailing words are read in any order. The new item still goes right after the slot's last word, #privacy, so after the state: FBL places a new word by the words of its slot and of the slots before it, and never moves the words already written (FBL 0.7 section 6.3). The designer writes tags first on a line it writes itself; a line written in another order keeps it.

steps.doc: addTag on REQ-0004 with the name user experience, typed with a space: the operation trims it and replaces the space with -, so the name is user-experience (hierarchical-requirement.des, addTag: p.name.trim().replace(' ', '-')), which no member has in any case, so the operation creates the tag at the end of the list and sets it on REQ-0004 (FR-027). The set is an insert-key of one space and #user-experience right after #self-service, the slot's last word, before state:proposed. The create of the Tag writes the registration in the same edit: hierarchical-requirement-tag-list shows those splices, for a registration with its tags block and for one without.

steps.doc: renameTag on the member security with the name infosec (FR-028): the operation sets the tags of every item and requirement that carries it, in any case, then the member's name, in one transaction, so one edit and one step of the history. The carriers are ITEM-0001, REQ-0001 and REQ-0003, in the order of the forEach over items, then requirements. Each changed item of the many slot tags is a replace-value of its word's group value, the name after # (FBL 0.7 section 6.3): Security on REQ-0003, spelt as its author wrote it, is replaced by infosec like the others. A tag is no reference (FBL section 5.7), so these are replace-value splices and not rewrite-reference ones. The member's new name writes the registration in the same edit: hierarchical-requirement-tag-list shows those splices. The fixture's edit holds the first change, x-transaction all four.
